Verify that surfaces are ready to receive work and that subfloor surface is clean, wired, and free of substances which could affect bond. B. Do not begin work until concrete substrate has cured 10 days minimum. C. Test concrete surface for negative alkalinity with litmus paper test. D. By beginning the work of this section, Subcontractor warrants it has examined and verified that the existing conditions are in accordance with the provisions of preceding paragraphs of subpart 3.01. 3.02 PREPARATION A. All surfaces to be coated shall be prepared in accordance with ASTM D 4258. Surface cleaning is intended to provide a clean contamination-free surface suitable for coating application. B. New concrete shall have a minimum ten (10) day cure at an average temperature of 73 degrees F., prior to coating. Concrete shall have a minimum 2500 psi. compressive of 270 psi. tensile strength. Surface of concrete shall have light broom, wood trowel or magnesium “bull” float finish. C. New concrete should be cured per ACI 308. No curing agents or sealers (such as silicon based sealers) shall be used that may interfere with the adhesion of the coating to be applied. D. All concrete surfaces shall be prepared per ASTM D 4259, Section 8; Abrasive Blast Cleaning Procedures. Prepare surface profile and remove laitance and solid contaminants from surface by abrasive blast cleaning. After blast cleaning, surface shall be free from curing compounds, surface glaze, laitance, salts, loosely adhering material, and foreign material of any kind. 1. Perform blasting operation so as to open any surface voids, bugholes, etc., and to remove curing compounds, surface glaze, laitance, salts, loosely adhering material, and foreign material of any kind. 2. Use only dry, oil-free air and clean media, unless other blast cleaning methods are approved. As-Built 09730-4 April 30, 2002 LLNL-TR-2004972 DWTF Phase 3B OCS-0069 3. After blast cleaning, completely remove dust and loose particles by vacuuming. Merely brushing or blowing will not be accepted. 4.
